definitions.explanation: The edge of a body of water — river, lake, or sea.

examples.japanese: {湖|みずうみ}の{岸辺|きしべ}に{立|た}った。
examples.english: I stood on the shore of the lake.

examples.japanese: {岸辺|きしべ}に{小|ちい}さなボートが{並|なら}んでいた。
examples.english: Small boats were lined up along the shore.

examples.japanese: {夕日|ゆうひ}に{照|て}らされた{岸辺|きしべ}の{風景|ふうけい}は、まるで{絵|え}のように{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: The shore lit up by the sunset was as beautiful as a painting.

notes:
Composed of {岸|きし} (shore, bank) + {辺|べ} (vicinity, edge). A somewhat literary word that can refer to the edge of any body of water. Has a poetic, evocative quality and appears frequently in literature and song titles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {湖|みずうみ}の{岸辺|きしべ}: lakeshore
- {川|かわ}の{岸辺|きしべ}: riverbank
- {岸辺|きしべ}に{打|う}ち{寄|よ}せる{波|なみ}: waves lapping at the shore
- {岸辺|きしべ}を{歩|ある}く: to walk along the shore

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {川辺|かわべ}: riverside — specifically for rivers
- {川岸|かわぎし}: riverbank — more concrete, the physical bank
- {海辺|うみべ}: seaside — specifically for the ocean
- {湖畔|こはん}: lakeside — specifically for lakes, often more formal
